name: Minimal Change Log
author: @opensmell
tagline: One array, one reference, one honest change.
summary: The smallest complete Vial: a sample log, a live ΔR/R₀ panel that declares host transforms and a tracked trajectory, and an explicit limit on what the array can claim.
whatItIs: A reference implementation of the Vial contract. It shows how a sandboxed fragment reads the host snapshot, declares transforms and a trajectory, and arms a single-unit watch only when a limit is entered.
whatItIsNot: It is not calibrated and not a scientific instrument. It does not identify compounds, quantify concentration, or compare readings from a different array.
citations: Janata, J. (2009). Principles of Chemical Sensors, 2nd ed. Springer. ISBN 978-0-387-69930-1.

widgets.title: Minimal Change Log
widgets.subtitle: The smallest thing that is still honest.
widgets.note: Reference Vial · sandboxed fragment · host-owned data

widgets.headline: A change is not a verdict.
widgets.body: The array responds to a mixture of volatiles. A reading says the sample changed on this rig; it does not say what changed.
always: Record the sample, the moment, and the conditions with every reading.
Compare only against a baseline taken on the same array and preparation.
never: Never treat a reading as an identification.
Never compare readings from a different array.

widgets.title: Sample log
widgets.description: The log is the record. The reading is one column in it.

rules.when: A reading moves and nothing you changed explains it
rules.then: Re-baseline on the same array and repeat the measurement before acting.

rules.when: A channel is dead, stuck, or saturated
rules.then: Stop. Repair or recalibrate before recording again.

widgets.title: Use this with your rig
widgets.body: Record a clean reference and a sample on the same array. Compare them in Check. If the arrays differ, the app refuses the comparison.

docs.title: How to use this Vial
body: Fill the sample and context fields, then add a reading whenever you measure or observe the sample.
The UI panel shows the host's own noise per channel. Enter a watch limit in ΔR/R₀ and arm it; the host refuses dead channels and non-live sources.

docs.title: What the array is doing
body: A MOX array responds to a mixture of volatile compounds. Temperature, humidity, distance, and sample preparation all change the reading.
The useful signal is a change relative to a reference on the same array. The absolute number does not transfer to another rig.
